name: Nucleotide Biosynthesis (Purine and Pyrimidine)
description: Nucleotide biosynthesis in E. coli produces purine (ATP, GTP) and pyrimidine (CTP, UTP, TTP) nucleotides for DNA and RNA synthesis. Purines are built on ribose-5-phosphate via 10-step pathway (PRPP to IMP to AMP/GMP). Pyrimidines are synthesized as free bases then attached to ribose (Asp + Carbamoyl-P to UMP, then CTP/TTP). Both pathways are regulated by end-product feedback inhibition and transcriptional control. The pathways branch at multiple points, use ATP/GTP for energy, and produce dNTPs via ribonucleotide reductase for DNA synthesis. This illustrates metabolic complexity with multiple OR gates for alternative substrates and branch points.
scientificAccuracy: Based on comprehensive biochemical characterization of E. coli nucleotide synthesis enzymes. All pathways validated.
